subject: Re: No-model-training commitment and DPA - Veridian Health integration
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@veridianhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: Initial question: training/data use commitments for Veridian integration

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for the demo last week — the team liked the latency profile. Before we move to procurement, our Legal & Privacy teams have a few non-negotiable asks around model training and data handling for the Veridian integration:

- A contractual "no-model-training" commitment (our patient diagnostic prompts/responses must not be used to improve models).
- Confirmation that prompts/responses are treated as customer-owned data (we need IP/ownership language).
- A current list of subprocessors and what data they may access.
- Details on cross-border transfer mechanisms (SCCs or equivalent) for EU/US flows.

Can you point me to the clause language you propose and any evidence (SOC 2, subprocessors list) we can attach to the DPA? If Redwood cannot offer a full no-train commitment, we need to understand the opt-out mechanism and technical controls.

Appreciate a quick reply — procurement wants to slot this into the quarter.

Best,
Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Integrations
Veridian Health

---

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2027 11:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial question: training/data use commitments for Veridian integration

Hi Elena —

Thanks for laying these out. Short answers up front: yes we can contractually offer a no-model-training commitment scoped to customer-provided prompts/responses; we maintain a subprocessors list and can provide SOC 2 Type II evidence; for EU data we rely on SCCs and customer-configurable region routing.

A few clarifying Qs so I can loop in Legal properly:
- Is the integration inbound only (Veridian calls Redwood APIs) or will Redwood be ingesting customer data from your S3 buckets?
- Do you need a clause that covers both development telemetry and production prompts/responses, or strictly production PII prompts?

I'll attach our DPA redline (v1) and the subprocessors export for your review — Legal can amend. If it helps, happy to do a 30-min working session with your counsel tomorrow.

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redline_v1.docx, subprocessors_list.csv

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Veridian - no-train ask + DPA redline (need legal language + risk call)

Folks — forwarding Veridian's ask. Key negotiation points I want Legal to consider:

1) No-model-training commitment: we can offer a clause that says "Customer data, including prompts and model outputs, will not be used to train or improve Redwood's models." We should include an exception for aggregated telemetry used strictly for service stability (no customer-identifying content).

2) Ownership: customer retains ownership of prompts/responses; Redwood will not assert IP rights over customer content.

3) Subprocessors: provide CSV of subprocessors and commit to 30-day notice before changes.

4) Cross-border transfers: offer SCCs + contractually require encryption at rest and customer-controlled region pinning where available.

Rishi — any concerns on the telemetry exception or inability to provide full segregation? Lauren — can you draft sample contract language for the no-train clause + a fallback (opt-out via API flag + billing/ops note)? Veridian wants this quick so propose we sync with their counsel tomorrow at 10am PT.

Thanks,
Jonas

---

From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@veridianhealth.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Veridian Health Legal <legal@veridianhealth.com>, Carlos Mendes <c.mendes@veridianhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Apr 2027 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian - no-train ask + DPA redline (need legal language + risk call)

Thanks Jonas —

Legal reviewed your summary and asked for two practical items ahead of the call:

- A redlined DPA with the proposed no-train clause included so their counsel can mark edits (they attached our standard questionnaire for context).
- Evidence of controls: SOC 2 report or a link to our dedicated security portal, and a clear statement whether subprocessors have access to plaintext prompts/responses.

I've attached Veridian_Security_Questionnaire.pdf for your reference. We are sensitive to the telemetry exception; Veridian's privacy team will not accept any telemetry that could be reconstructed into customer prompts. If telemetry is unavoidable for stability, we need a technical description of fields collected and the retention window.

Can you provide the redline and SOC 2 link before our proposed 10am PT call tomorrow?

Best,
Elena

Attachment: Veridian_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

---

From: jonas_weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@veridianhealth.com>, Veridian Health Legal <legal@veridianhealth.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Apr 2027 08:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Veridian - DPA redline + evidence (see attachments + call notes)

Elena / team —

Thanks for the questionnaire — attached is Redwood_DPA_redline_v2.docx which includes: a contractual no-model-training clause that applies to customer-provided prompts/responses; explicit customer ownership language; a telemetry carve-out limited to "service stability metrics" (latency, CPU/memory, anonymized perf histograms) retained for no more than 30 days and never tied back to customer identifiers.

Subprocessor access: our subprocessors operate at the infrastructure and observability layer; we have implemented encryption at rest and in transit. Subprocessors do not receive plaintext prompt/response content unless you opt into a managed integration that requires file ingestion to your dedicated bucket (we'd only do that with explicit written consent). See subprocessors_list.csv for names and roles.

Evidence: SOC 2 Type II report is available via our security portal (link below).

Next steps:
- If that language looks OK, we'll circulate the DocuSign packet (link below) for legal and procurement.
- If you require a strict "no telemetry" guarantee, we can add a stricter clause but it may limit some runtime diagnostics and we should document the operational tradeoffs.

DocuSign (draft): https://www.docusign.com/sign/REDWOOD-VER-042
Security portal / SOC2: https://security.redwoodinference.com/reports/REDWOOD-SOC2-2026

Attachments: Redwood_DPA_redline_v2.docx, subprocessors_list.csv

Happy to jump on the call at 10am PT.

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Jonas —

Thanks for the thorough response and the updated redline. Legal is comfortable with the proposed no-model-training clause and the telemetry carve-out as described, provided we get the specific telemetry fields and the 30-day retention written into the DPA appendix (they noted this will be a conditional acceptance). Procurement wants the signed DocuSign packet; I'll route the draft to our procurement lead today.

One last ask: please confirm whether Redwood will notify us 30 days before any processor change that could affect prompt/response handling. If yes, we can proceed to sign.

If all good, expect signatures by end of next week.

Regards,
Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Integrations
Veridian Health
